verdict.rationale: ReadMe documents Markdown authoring with MDX support, including JSX syntax. It also ships some built-in rich elements, such as Mermaid diagrams inserted via a slash command and Font Awesome icons, and lets authors build custom MDX components. None of the evidence names the specific components the story asks for, so it is unproven that tabs, callouts, code groups and steps come without custom work. Missing for 10: documented built-in tabs, callouts, code groups and steps components; independent or hands-on confirmation of authoring them without custom HTML.

support.subject: As a technical writer, I author pages in Markdown/MDX with rich components — tabs, callouts, code groups, steps — without writing custom HTML

citations.quote: Write MDX in ReadMe, including the JSX syntax and the places where it behaves differently from plain Markdown.
Write long-form tutorials, walkthroughs, and explanations that sit beside your API Reference, in Markdown with MDX support.
Add flowcharts, sequence diagrams, and other Mermaid diagrams to your docs with a slash command, written as text rather than images.
build fully custom MDX components beyond GitBook's block editor
